inputs.root_cause: Both SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C632C43201760C05 (XLIFF-INLINE-001) and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C6C67E6C253C9EAB (XLIFF-PARSE-001)'s own missing_behavior text already named this exact gap: 'The <data> element's own REQUIRED id attribute is not separately enforced as a validate() diagnostic if absent (only downstream dataRef resolution against present ids is checked).' Read the pinned core schema directly and confirmed <xs:attribute name="id" use="required" type="xs:NMTOKEN"/> on the <data> element. _data_ref_diagnostics's data_ids set silently excluded any <data> element with a missing id, so no diagnostic was ever raised for the <data> element itself violating its own required attribute.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C632C43201760C05 and SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C6C67E6C253C9EAB (both partial) -- remain partial; evidence strengthened, real bug fixed, no status crossing
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 2 new tests prove: a <data> element missing its id is flagged with xliff.originalData.data.id.missing; a normal document with all ids present is unaffected.
inputs.regression_tier: full xliff package suite (tests/python/xliff) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. After four consecutive resource-limit/version-gate fixes across xliff/ora/nrrd, surveyed ORA's remaining 5 partial obligations (found correctly blocked on large missing subsystems) and then xliff's remaining 27 partial obligations directly, per the 'read each partial obligation's own missing_behavior text for an already-diagnosed narrow gap' technique proven at event 250 against nrrd.

2. Found SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C632C43201760C05 and its sibling SAL-XLIFF-OBL-C6C67E6C253C9EAB's own missing_behavior text already named a concrete, narrow, spec-grounded second half of a two-part gap: the <cp> child-element modeling half is explicitly NOT a gap for this obligation's own rule_text (already correctly scoped out), but the <data> element's own REQUIRED id attribute enforcement genuinely is.

3. Read the pinned core schema directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xlf-002.bin, schemas/xliff_core_2.0.xsd) and confirmed <xs:attribute name="id" use="required" type="xs:NMTOKEN"/> on the <data> element definition.

4. Read _data_ref_diagnostics (validator.py) directly and found data_ids = {value.id for value in unit.original_data if value.id} -- a <data> element with a missing/empty id is silently filtered OUT of the set with no diagnostic raised for the <data> element itself.

5. Confirmed this is a genuine, exploitable gap via direct probing before any fix: loaded a unit with one <data> element missing its id attribute and validated it -- no diagnostic named that element or its missing required attribute at all.

6. Added a dedicated check at the top of _data_ref_diagnostics that enumerates unit.original_data and flags every <data> element with a missing/empty id as xliff.originalData.data.id.missing, before the existing dataRef-resolution logic runs.
7. Re-probed both cases: a unit with a <data> element missing id now raises xliff.originalData.data.id.missing; a unit with all ids present raises no such diagnostic.
8. Ran the full pre-existing xliff suite (470 tests, zero new fixtures) against the fix to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 470 passed unchanged.
9. Wrote 2 formal tests in the existing test_obligation_original_data_element_modeling.py (extending its established _document() helper pattern), both passing on the first attempt.

10. Ran ruff (clean), the full xliff suite (472 passed, was 470, +2), and the full 6-format regression (3448 passed, was 3446, +2; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

11. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-fbb0b7f547e83ece, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

12. Both obligations remain status=partial: their missing_behavior now lists only the already-correctly-scoped-out <cp> modeling non-gap. This tick strengthens evidence with a real, previously-unnoticed required-attribute enforcement gap fixed (the exact gap both obligations' own text already named), rather than crossing a status boundary.
